answer: Call it ivory-tower theory. A farm will simply wait it out, you say. Waiting is the price, though. A newcomer wears a saffron mark in the public record until it finishes a stretch of low-paid work anyone can inspect, work whose receipts echo real jobs done for real clients. Running a thousand fake identities costs a farm a thousand stretches of earning nothing. Real newcomers wait too, and that is the honest cost.
